analogies.relation: A garrulous person talks excessively, as a gluttonous person eats excessively.

A recluse seeks out solitude, as a socialite seeks out company.

A hypocrite characteristically dissembles, as a braggart characteristically boasts.
A fugitive is defined by absconding, as a stowaway is defined by hiding.
A heckler's role is to deride, as a cheerleader's role is to encourage.
A chronicler documents events, as a cartographer maps territory.
A sage's function is to counsel, as a jester's function is to amuse.
Something soporific induces drowsiness, as something hilarious induces laughter.
A catalyst sets off a reaction, as a spark sets off a fire.
To enervate is to drain something of vigor, as to deflate is to drain something of air.
Blood thickens into clumps when it coagulates, as milk thickens into clumps when it curdles.
To foment a rebellion is to stir it up, as to fan flames is to make them grow.
A levee protects against a flood, as an umbrella protects against rain.
A buttress supports a wall, as a trellis supports a vine.
A strut is a structural member of a framework, as a spoke is a structural member of a wheel.
A shard is a sharp broken fragment of glass, as a splinter is a sharp broken fragment of wood.
A coda is the concluding section of a symphony, as an epilogue is the concluding section of a novel.
A log is the official record of a voyage, as minutes are the official record of a meeting.
An itinerary is a plan made before a journey, as a blueprint is a plan made before a building.
A dirge is a song that expresses grief, as an anthem is a song that expresses patriotism.
A eulogy is a speech that expresses praise, as an apology is a statement that expresses regret.
To burnish something is to give it a shine, as to whet something is to give it an edge.
Distilling extracts an essence from a substance, as pressing extracts juice from fruit.
Ephemeral and perennial are opposites, as are temporary and permanent.
To exculpate is to free someone from blame, as to absolve is to free someone from sin.
Tractable and recalcitrant are opposites, as are docile and unruly.
Diffidence and effrontery are opposites, as are timidity and boldness.
To prevaricate is to evade the truth, as to dodge is to evade a blow.
A quibble is a petty objection, as a squabble is a petty argument.
A stigma is a mark of disgrace, as a medal is a mark of valor.
A precursor is by definition one who precedes, as an heir is by definition one who inherits.
An ascetic renounces luxury, as a vegetarian renounces meat.
Something impervious cannot be penetrated, as someone invincible cannot be defeated.
Someone implacable cannot be appeased, as a mark that is indelible cannot be erased.
Something malleable is easy to shape, as something flexible is easy to bend.
An officious person tends to meddle, as a nosy person tends to pry.
A contrite person feels remorse, as a nostalgic person feels longing.
An irascible person is easily moved to anger, as a squeamish person is easily moved to disgust.
A gullible person is easily deceived, as a fragile object is easily broken.
Someone inured to hardship has grown used to it, as someone acclimated to a climate has grown used to it.
To satiate an appetite is to satisfy it fully, as to quench a thirst is to satisfy it fully.
Adulterating something lowers its purity, as diluting something lowers its strength.
To impede is to block progress, as to obstruct is to block a view.
To rescind a law is to take it back, as to retract a statement is to take it back.
To disseminate information is to spread it widely, as to scatter seeds is to spread them widely.
A gland's function is to secrete, as a heart's function is to pump.
Syrup is typically viscous, as glass is typically brittle.
A pungent smell is sharp and intense, as a shrill sound is sharp and intense.
Something luminous gives off light, as something fragrant gives off scent.
An iconoclastic person attacks convention, as a rebellious person defies authority.

An anachronism is an error in time, as a misnomer is an error in name.
A metamorphosis is a change of form, as a relocation is a change of place.
Chicanery is the characteristic practice of a trickster, as larceny is the characteristic practice of a thief.
A fledgling is a young bird, as a sapling is a young tree.
